text:
maya: Heads-up — canary run for continuous-batching (short seq workload) shows a surprising p50 regression: baseline 34ms -> canary 47ms, p95 also shifted. nvtx/nsys traces attached in the run but quick summary below. :frowning:

priya: Which change in canary? matmul fusion landed last week right?

maya: Yes, matmul-fusion PR (rev abc123) merged 2026-03-10. I profiled with nsys and perfetto. Timeline shows repeated kernel-selector churn: large-matmul (fast on big batches) gets picked, then immediately a memcpy+kernel for small-matmul happens, then back — this oscillation correlates with increased queue-to-compute time. Also seeing host->device memcpy spikes (~0.6-1.2ms every 10-20ms window) that line up with KV cache prefetches.

sam: Can you paste the nsys command / snippet you used?

maya: Sure — ran with minimal app wrapper and NVTX around routing + serve loop: 
```
nsys profile -o out_canary --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=cpu --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi \
  -- ./bin/inference_canary --workload mixed_short_seqs --batch-window-ms=6 
```
Timeline clip (condensed):
```
[0ms] host: accept request x3
[1ms] selector: choose kernel large-matmul
[1.2ms] cudaMemcpy H2D (prefetch KV) 0.9ms
[2.2ms] kernel: large-matmul 2.1ms
[4.3ms] selector: choose kernel small-matmul
[4.35ms] kernel: small-matmul 0.7ms
[5.05ms] cudaMemcpy H2D (prefetch KV) 1.1ms
[6.15ms] kernel: large-matmul 2.0ms
```
Look at the selector decision frequency — it's switching mid-window because prefetches change effective batch shape. That interaction expands observed queue time (host-side) while GPU sees more frequent small kernels + memcpy, hurting throughput and tail latency.

kevin: Huh. Our selector currently scores kernels by estimated batch_size * mean_seq_len and picks max score; it doesn't consider batch shape variance or host-copy penalty. If prefetches intermittently enlarge the window, the heuristic will flip.

priya: Quick experiment — I pushed selector tweak to branch `selector/variance-penalty` that adds a small penalty term: penalty = alpha * stddev_seq_len + beta * h2d_ms_estimate. With alpha=0.7, beta=1.1 I re-ran the 10m canary and p50 dropped to 36ms (almost baseline). GPU utilization slightly lower but tail improved.

sam: Nice. Do you have the exact config snippet?

priya: Yep: 
```json
{"batch_window_ms": 6, "kernel_selector": {"score_fn": "bs*mean_seq - 0.7*seq_std - 1.1*h2d_ms"}}
```
(we use a simple linear model for now; h2d_ms is estimated from recent memcpy samples)

maya: I also tried lowering BATCH_WINDOW_MS from 6 -> 3 on the canary without selector changes: that reduced host memcpy overlap but increased number of kernel launches which raised GPU kernel overhead; p50 ended up ~40ms. So combined approach (window 5 + selector penalty) seems best for this workload.

kevin: Two follow-ups: 1) add a metric for "kernel-swap-rate" (selector picks different kernel across consecutive requests) and alert if > X/sec; 2) record h2d_ms rolling average in the telemetry so selector can make decisions without full trace.

maya: Agreed. I'll add a lightweight sampler in runtime to push h2d_ms to telemetry and add the kernel-swap-rate counter. We'll run 2hr canary with selector/variance-penalty + batch_window_ms=5.

perf-bot: perf-bot: scheduled nsys comparators: baseline vs selector/variance-penalty vs window-3. Expecting artifacts in ~55min, will post summary. :eyes:

sam: One more note — double-check driver/CUDA minor version: on one host I reproduced a slightly different memcpy timing that made beta need retuning. If we see noisy h2d_ms across machines we should normalize by device micro-benchmarks.

priya: Good call. I'll add a tiny memcpy microbench at startup to calibrate the h2d estimator.

maya: Thanks all. For the postmortem: root cause = selector heuristic insufficiently aware of batch-shape variance + KV prefetch memcpy pattern causing mid-window shape flips -> kernel thrash + host memcpy bursts -> increased p50. Short-term mitigations: selector penalty + reduce window slightly. Long-term: richer selector model + per-host memcpy calibration + telemetry alerting.

kevin: Sounds good. Tagging this for 2nd-pass perf doc and an RFC if fixes hold in the canary. :+1:

perf-bot: perf-bot: results uploaded to /run_artifacts/1793001111/netsummary.html (will link in thread when ready).
